title: Introduce work-stealing request executor to reduce main-thread scheduling jank
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: production traces show recurring main-thread scheduling spikes and long tail latency during high-concurrency inference bursts. Root cause analysis identified contention on a single global executor state, frequent syscall-based handoffs, and suboptimal work distribution when serving mixed short/long sequences. This change introduces a work-stealing request executor: per-worker ring buffers plus light-weight stealable queues, adaptive batch stealing for continuous batching, and a lock-free request marshalling path to eliminate main-thread syscalls for the happy path. The patch also shards the in-memory KV cache by CPU core and adds a small probabilistic sampler for tracing steal events. Highlights: 1) New executor package with WorkPool and Stealer implementations that implement adaptive backpressure and fairness thresholds. 2) Lock-free ring buffer for request frames to remove mutex hot paths on enqueue/dequeue. 3) Per-core KV cache shards with fast-path inline lookup to reduce cross-core cacheline bouncing. 4) Batch stealing logic that allows workers to pull partial batches from peers to keep GPU feeding steady without central coordination. 5) Metrics and traces for steal counts, steal latency, and local-vs-remote-batch sizes. Note: kept compatibility with existing scheduler APIs; feature is opt-in behind runtime flag runtime.executor=work-steal so we can roll out via canary. Benchmark summary: microbenchmarks show 11-18% lower p50 CPU request latency under 1k concurrent connections and 20-27% reduction in p99 under mixed short/long workloads. End-to-end perf tests with continuous batching enabled show a 9% token throughput improvement at SLO-bound latency. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-7284) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] benchmark harness updates - [x] metrics and dashboards skeleton - [x] docs/notes for canary rollout What changed (high level): added pkg/runtime/executor/workpool.go, pkg/runtime/executor/steal.go, pkg/runtime/serialization/ringbuf.go, pkg/runtime/kv/cache_shard.go, bench/cpu/steal_bench.go, tests/integration/exec_pool_test.go, docs/perf/work-stealing.md; updated runtime/config/defaults.go to add flag. Rollout plan: enable feature in Canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic for 24 hours, collect steal metrics and error rates, then 50% for 6 hours, then full rollout if no regressions. Related: follows up on ENG-4123 and reuses some ideas from the earlier request-executor refactors. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to memory reclamation in ringbuf and ensure steal path latency is instrumented.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Overall looks promising. Can you add metrics for local enqueue/dequeue wait time and a histogram for steal batch sizes? Also please show unit tests exercising wraparound for the ring buffer.
Aisha Patel: Added enqueue/dequeue wait metrics and tests for ringbuf wraparound. Instrumented steal batch-size histogram. See new commits that update tests and metrics registration.
Sofia Martinez: I'm concerned about memory churn when partial batches are stolen repeatedly. Could we bound the number of steals per attempt?
Aisha Patel: Implemented a steal cap and exponential backoff when steals repeatedly fail to acquire tokens. Updated docs to describe backoff behavior.
Evan Brooks: Integration tests passed locally but I saw a sporadic flake where a worker deadlocked in teardown in race builds. Can you add a graceful shutdown path?
Aisha Patel: Added graceful shutdown token and fixed a race in worker exit path. Verified with -race in CI.
Daniel Kim: Approved after metric names are stable and benchmarks attached. Left a small nit on a comment block.
Sofia Martinez: Approved. Verified dashboards in staging show expected steal rates and no error regression.
checks_summary: bench/latency: p50 -11% p99 -22% on mixed workloads
release_notes: Introduce opt-in work-stealing executor to reduce CPU-side scheduling latency and improve throughput. Default behavior unchanged; enable with runtime.executor=work-steal. Observed p99 reductions in mixed workloads and improved steady-state throughput. Monitor steal metrics when rolling out.
notes: Feature gated and rolled out via canary. No infra changes required for default deployments. Follow rollout plan in docs/perf/work-stealing.md for safe enablement.
